correctness.rationale: For n>=4 in H_n obtained by subdividing each K_n edge once, verified original-to-original distance 2, original-to-edge vertex distance 1 or 3, and edge-to-edge distance 2 (intersecting old edges) or 4 (disjoint). Neighbor maximality then identifies MMD pairs exactly as pairs of subdivision vertices representing disjoint old edges; every original vertex is isolated in the strong resolving graph. By standard strong resolving graph/vertex cover equivalence, inclusion-minimal strong resolvers are exactly complements among the C(n,2) edge vertices of maximal pairwise-intersecting 2-subsets of [n]. Such families are precisely all n full stars and C(n,3) triangles: a nonstar intersecting family contains the sides of a triangle and no further 2-set. Consequently R_n(z)=n z^(C(n,2)-n+1)+C(n,3) z^(C(n,2)-3); the two cardinalities differ by n-4 and all intermediate sizes absent. Independent shortest-path BFS MMD and exhaustive maximal intersecting family checks at n=4..6 returned 8,15,26 sets as expected; the n>=4 proof is structural.
residual_risks: Small n=4..6 checks do not prove all orders; proof uses MMD classification and classical maximal intersecting 2-set lemma.

value.rationale: The strong resolving sets of the complete graph incidence subdivision are a natural obstruction family. Identifying their minimal covers with maximal intersecting 2-subset families gives a complete two-term labelled polynomial and the unbounded gap n-5 of impossible intermediate cardinalities; neither the minimum strong metric dimension nor generic algorithms describe this distribution. This sharp family-level classification has stand-alone utility despite its use of classical intersecting-set structure.
